title: How do we recreate the house with every border line five centimetres?
description: The house figure is rebuilt with a ruler, a set square and a compass, and every line of its border is five centimetres. Keeko's doubt is that one arc from B is enough to find the top point, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the top point is five centimetres from both B and C, so it is found where an arc from B meets an arc from C. Watch for students who draw only one arc.

source: Recreate this house figure. All the lines forming the border
video_script.why: A learner rebuilds a figure in an order that places each point from points already drawn, finding the top point from two compass arcs.
video_script.substitution: the book's house with the base DE of five centimetres, the walls DB and EC, the roof sides AB and AC, and the arc from B to C
video_script.anchor: the book's house with the base DE, the walls DB and EC, the roof meeting at A, and the curved arc from B to C
video_script.wrong_answer: one arc from bee is enough to find the top point
video_script.wrong_move: draws one arc and picks any point on it, though only one point of that arc is also five centimetres from cee
video_script.payoff_line: The house is ready, with every border line five centimetres long.

final_answer.value: a house with DE = DB = EC = AB = AC = 5 cm, a door 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall, and an arc from B to C with centre A
final_answer.spoken: the house is ready, with every border line five centimetres long

maths_rules: the base DE is 5 cm, and the walls DB and EC are perpendicular to DE and 5 cm each
the door is 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall on the base
A is 5 cm from B and 5 cm from C, so it is where an arc from B meets an arc from C
the arc from B to C is drawn with centre A and radius 5 cm
BC = 5 cm as well, so AB = AC = BC
video_script.design: The house is built on the board in four steps, each new line in a new colour. The two arcs for the top point stay visible until the roof is joined.

beats.on_screen: title card, then the house figure with every border line marked 5 cm

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the house figure is drawn
marks.five: each border line is marked five centimetres

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about recreating a house figure.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Every line forming its border is five centimetres long.
In what order will you draw it?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the house with its points D, E, B, C and A named; the top point A is circled

marks.names: the points D, E, B and C are named on the house
marks.top: the top point A is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='names'/>The base is dee ee. The walls are dee bee and ee cee, and the roof meets at eigh.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The top point eigh is the one we do not yet know how to place.

beats.on_screen: Given: all the border lines are 5 cm; a door 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall on the base
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, all the border lines are five centimetres. The door is one centimetre wide and two centimetres tall.

marks.find: the task is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to recreate this house.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw the base DE = 5 cm; perpendiculars at D and E; mark B and C each 5 cm up; draw the door

marks.base: the base DE of 5 cm is drawn with perpendiculars at D and E
marks.walls: B and C are marked 5 cm up and the door is drawn on DE

narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>Step one, draw the base dee ee of five centimetres, with perpendiculars at dee and ee.
<bookmark mark='walls'/>Mark bee and cee five centimetres up. Then draw the door on the base.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: with the compass at 5 cm draw an arc from B and an arc from C; they meet at A

marks.arcb: an arc of 5 cm is drawn from B
marks.arcc: an arc of 5 cm is drawn from C and the two arcs meet at A

narration: <bookmark mark='arcb'/>Step two, set the compass to five centimetres. Draw an arc from bee.
<bookmark mark='arcc'/>With the same opening, draw an arc from cee. The two arcs meet at eigh.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: join AB and AC; with the compass point at A and radius 5 cm draw the arc from B to C

marks.roof: A is joined to B and to C
marks.curve: the arc from B to C is drawn with centre A

narration: <bookmark mark='roof'/>Step three, join eigh bee and eigh cee.
<bookmark mark='curve'/>Put the compass point on eigh with radius five centimetres. Draw the arc from bee to cee.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check AB = AC = 5 cm; since BC = 5 cm as well, all three sides of ABC are equal

marks.check: AB and AC are measured 5 cm and BC is measured 5 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check that eigh bee and eigh cee are both five centimetres. Bee cee is also five centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the house is ready; DE = DB = EC = AB = AC = 5 cm

marks.res: every border line is ticked as 5 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The house is ready, with every border line five centimetres long.
<bookmark mark='res'/>The top point eigh is five centimetres from both bee and cee.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the house
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble 'one arc from B' struck out; one arc from B with several dots on it, only one of them also 5 cm from C

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears beside the arc from B
marks.fix: several dots are marked on the arc from B, and only one of them is also 5 cm from C
marks.keep: the bubble is struck out and the second arc from C is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one arc from bee is enough to find the top point.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But an arc from bee holds many points that are five centimetres from bee.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Only one of them is also five centimetres from cee, and the second arc finds it.
